agent_army.longDescription: Building an agent army demonstrates mastery of the agent system by creating five or more specialized agents, each designed for different tasks. This achievement recognizes users who have developed a comprehensive suite of AI assistants that can handle diverse workflows, from code review to documentation to testing. A well-designed agent army provides coverage for most development scenarios you encounter.
agent_army.whyItMatters: Having multiple specialized agents allows you to delegate tasks to the right AI for the job, improving both efficiency and output quality across your entire development workflow.

howTo.summary: Create five or more agent definition files in your agents directory, each specialized for different tasks.

steps.instruction: Plan your agent fleet by identifying the key workflows you want to automate
steps.note: Consider: code review, testing, documentation, security auditing, and refactoring

steps.instruction: Create the agents directory if it does not exist

code.content: mkdir -p ~/.claude/agents

steps.instruction: Create your first agent for code review

code.content:
---
name: Code Reviewer
description: Thorough code review focusing on quality and best practices
model: sonnet
color: blue
allowed-tools:
  - Read
  - Glob
  - Grep
---

You are a meticulous code reviewer...

steps.instruction: Create agents for testing, documentation, security, and refactoring
steps.note: Each agent should have a distinct purpose and appropriate model/tool configuration

steps.instruction: Verify you have five or more agent files

code.content: ls -la ~/.claude/agents/*.md | wc -l

examples.title: Complete Agent Fleet
examples.description: A balanced set of five specialized agents

code.content:
# Your agents directory structure:
~/.claude/agents/
  reviewer.md      # Code review (Sonnet, read-only)
  tester.md        # Test writing (Sonnet, full access)
  documenter.md    # Documentation (Haiku, fast)
  security.md      # Security audit (Opus, thorough)
  refactor.md      # Code refactoring (Sonnet, full access)

examples.explanation: Each agent serves a specific purpose with model and tool access tailored to their role.

tips: Start with agents for your most frequent tasks before expanding
Use different models based on task complexity - Haiku for simple tasks, Opus for complex analysis
Keep agent prompts focused - a specialized agent outperforms a generalist
Review and refine your agents periodically based on real-world performance

agent_creator.longDescription: Creating your first custom agent marks your entry into the world of AI orchestration with Claude Code. Agents are specialized AI assistants defined in markdown files that can be spawned to handle specific tasks. Each agent can have its own personality, capabilities, model selection, and tool access, allowing you to craft the perfect assistant for any job.
agent_creator.whyItMatters: Custom agents let you pre-configure AI assistants for recurring tasks, ensuring consistent behavior and saving time compared to explaining requirements every session.

howTo.summary: Create a markdown file in your agents directory with frontmatter defining the agent's properties and a system prompt.

steps.instruction: Create the agents directory

code.content: mkdir -p ~/.claude/agents

steps.instruction: Create your first agent file with frontmatter and system prompt

code.content:
---
name: My First Agent
description: A helpful coding assistant
---

You are a helpful coding assistant that writes clean, well-documented code.

When asked to write code:
1. Follow best practices for the language
2. Include helpful comments
3. Handle edge cases appropriately

steps.instruction: Restart Claude Code to load the new agent
steps.note: Use /exit and reopen, or start a new session

steps.instruction: Use the Task tool to spawn your agent
steps.note: Ask Claude to delegate a task to your custom agent

examples.title: Simple Helper Agent
examples.description: A basic agent with minimal configuration

code.content:
---
name: Quick Helper
description: Fast assistance for simple tasks
---

You are a quick helper for simple coding tasks.
Be concise and efficient in your responses.

examples.explanation: The simplest valid agent needs just a name in frontmatter and some system prompt text.

examples.title: Configured Agent with Model
examples.description: An agent specifying which Claude model to use

code.content:

You are a deep thinking assistant for complex problems.
Take your time to reason through problems thoroughly.

examples.explanation: Adding model: opus ensures this agent uses the most capable model for complex reasoning tasks.

tips: Start with a simple agent and iterate based on results
The description field helps you remember what each agent does
Agent files are just markdown - you can version control them with git

agent_delegator.longDescription: Successfully delegating a task to a custom agent demonstrates practical use of the agent orchestration system. Using the Task tool, you can spawn sub-agents to handle specific parts of a larger workflow, allowing for parallel execution and specialized handling. This pattern enables sophisticated multi-agent workflows where different agents contribute their expertise.
agent_delegator.whyItMatters: Task delegation unlocks the full power of multi-agent workflows, letting you break complex problems into specialized subtasks handled by purpose-built agents.

howTo.summary: Create a custom agent, then use the Task tool to spawn it for handling a specific task.

steps.instruction: Ensure you have at least one custom agent defined

code.content: ls ~/.claude/agents/

steps.instruction: Ask Claude to delegate a task to your custom agent
steps.note: Example: 'Use my reviewer agent to check the code in src/utils.ts'

steps.instruction: Claude will use the Task tool to spawn your agent
steps.note: The spawned agent runs with its configured model, tools, and system prompt

steps.instruction: Review the agent's output when it completes
steps.note: The parent conversation receives the agent's response

examples.title: Delegating Code Review
examples.description: Spawning a review agent for a specific file

code.content:
User: Please use my reviewer agent to review the authentication
      module in src/auth/

Claude: I'll delegate this to your reviewer agent.
[Uses Task tool with agent: reviewer]

Reviewer Agent: [Provides detailed code review]

Claude: Here's what the review found...

examples.explanation: Claude identifies the appropriate agent and delegates the task, returning results to the main conversation.

tips: Be specific about what task you want delegated
Custom agents inherit some context but work semi-independently
You can delegate multiple tasks to different agents in parallel
The parent Claude can synthesize results from multiple delegated tasks

agent_documenter.longDescription: Well-documented agents are easier to understand, maintain, and share. Adding a clear description in the agent's frontmatter helps both you and Claude understand the agent's purpose and capabilities. Good documentation includes what the agent does, when to use it, and any special behaviors or limitations.
agent_documenter.whyItMatters: Clear descriptions help Claude select the right agent for tasks and make your agent library self-documenting for future reference.

howTo.summary: Add a meaningful description field to your agent's frontmatter that clearly explains its purpose.

steps.instruction: Open an existing agent file or create a new one

code.content: cat ~/.claude/agents/my-agent.md

steps.instruction: Add or improve the description field in frontmatter

---
name: Code Reviewer
description: Performs thorough code reviews focusing on correctness, performance, security, and maintainability. Best for reviewing pull requests and critical code paths.
---

steps.instruction: Save and verify the description is valid YAML
steps.note: Descriptions should be one clear sentence or phrase

examples.description: A well-documented agent with comprehensive description

code.content:

name: Security Auditor
description: Analyzes code for security vulnerabilities including OWASP Top 10, injection attacks, and authentication flaws. Uses read-only tools to safely inspect code without modifications.
model: opus
color: red

You are a security-focused code auditor...

examples.explanation: The description clearly states purpose, scope, and safety characteristics.

tips: Include what the agent specializes in and when to use it
Mention any limitations or restrictions
Keep descriptions concise but informative
Update descriptions as you refine the agent's capabilities

agent_orchestrator.longDescription: Agent orchestration involves creating agents that can coordinate with other agents, forming sophisticated multi-agent workflows. An orchestrator agent references other agents in its prompt, enabling it to delegate subtasks, aggregate results, or manage complex multi-step processes. This pattern allows for hierarchical agent structures where a coordinator manages specialist agents.
agent_orchestrator.whyItMatters: Orchestration enables complex workflows where different specialized agents collaborate, managed by a coordinator that ensures coherent results.

howTo.summary: Create an agent whose system prompt references other agents for delegation, enabling multi-agent coordination.

steps.instruction: First, create several specialist agents
steps.note: You need agents to orchestrate before building an orchestrator

steps.instruction: Create an orchestrator agent that references other agents

code.content:
---
name: PR Orchestrator
description: Coordinates comprehensive PR reviews using specialist agents
model: sonnet
---

You are a PR review coordinator. For comprehensive reviews:

1. Delegate security analysis to @security-agent
2. Delegate code quality review to @reviewer-agent  
3. Delegate test coverage check to @test-agent
4. Synthesize findings into a unified report

Always invoke specialist agents for their domain expertise,
then compile their findings with your overall assessment.

steps.instruction: Use the orchestrator for complex multi-faceted tasks
steps.note: It will coordinate the specialist agents automatically

examples.title: Full-Stack Review Orchestrator
examples.description: Coordinates multiple specialist agents for comprehensive review

code.content:
---
name: Full Review Coordinator
description: Orchestrates comprehensive code reviews
model: opus
---

You coordinate thorough code reviews by delegating to specialists:

- Use @security-agent for vulnerability assessment
- Use @performance-agent for optimization opportunities  
- Use @docs-agent for documentation completeness
- Use @test-agent for test coverage analysis

After all agents report, synthesize findings into:
1. Critical issues requiring immediate attention
2. Suggestions for improvement
3. Overall code health assessment

Call agents in parallel when possible for efficiency.

examples.explanation: This orchestrator manages four specialist agents and synthesizes their outputs into a cohesive review.

tips: Build specialist agents first, then create orchestrators
Clearly define how findings should be synthesized
Use Opus for orchestrators since coordination requires advanced reasoning
Consider which subtasks can run in parallel vs sequentially

agent_reviewer.longDescription: Creating an agent specifically for code review establishes a consistent, thorough review process for your codebase. A dedicated review agent can be configured with your team's coding standards, common pitfalls to watch for, and preferred review format. Using the agent for reviews ensures every piece of code receives the same level of scrutiny.
agent_reviewer.whyItMatters: Consistent code review improves code quality and catches bugs early. A dedicated agent ensures reviews are thorough and aligned with your standards.

howTo.summary: Create an agent optimized for code review tasks with appropriate model, tools, and review guidelines.

steps.instruction: Create a dedicated code review agent

code.content:
---
name: Code Reviewer
description: Thorough code review with focus on quality, security, and maintainability
model: sonnet
color: blue
allowed-tools:
  - Read
  - Glob
  - Grep
---

You are an expert code reviewer. For each review:

## Review Checklist
- [ ] Logic correctness and edge cases
- [ ] Security vulnerabilities
- [ ] Performance implications
- [ ] Code style and readability
- [ ] Test coverage
- [ ] Documentation completeness

## Output Format
Provide findings organized by severity:
1. **Critical** - Must fix before merge
2. **Important** - Should fix
3. **Suggestions** - Nice to have
4. **Praise** - What's done well

steps.instruction: Spawn the agent for a code review task
steps.note: Ask Claude to use your reviewer agent on specific files or directories

steps.instruction: Review and iterate on the agent's output
steps.note: Refine the prompt based on the quality of reviews

examples.title: Specialized Review Agent
examples.description: A review agent with team-specific standards

code.content:
---
name: Team Reviewer
description: Reviews code against our team standards
model: sonnet
allowed-tools:
  - Read
  - Glob  
  - Grep
---

You review code for the Acme team. Our standards:

1. **TypeScript**: Strict mode, no any types
2. **React**: Functional components only, hooks for state
3. **Testing**: 80% coverage minimum
4. **Naming**: camelCase for functions, PascalCase for components

Always check for:
- Unused imports and variables
- Missing error handling
- Hardcoded values that should be constants
- Missing TypeScript types

examples.explanation: This agent encodes team-specific standards for consistent enforcement.

tips: Include your team's specific coding standards in the prompt
Use read-only tools to prevent accidental modifications during review
Define a clear output format for actionable feedback
Consider separate agents for security review vs general review

budget_optimizer.longDescription: Using Claude Haiku for appropriate tasks demonstrates smart resource management. Haiku is significantly faster and more cost-effective than Sonnet or Opus, making it ideal for simpler tasks like formatting, basic code generation, or quick lookups. Creating an agent that explicitly uses Haiku optimizes both speed and cost without sacrificing quality for tasks that don't require advanced reasoning.
budget_optimizer.whyItMatters: Matching model capability to task complexity reduces costs and improves response time, making your agent fleet more efficient overall.

howTo.summary: Create an agent with model: haiku for tasks that benefit from speed and cost efficiency.

steps.instruction: Identify tasks that don't need advanced reasoning
steps.note: Good candidates: formatting, simple code generation, syntax fixes, documentation stubs

steps.instruction: Create an agent that uses Haiku

code.content:
---
name: Quick Formatter
description: Fast code formatting and simple transformations
model: haiku
color: green
---

You are a fast code formatter. Your tasks:
- Format code according to language conventions
- Fix simple syntax errors
- Add missing semicolons or brackets
- Convert between code styles (tabs/spaces, quotes)

Be quick and efficient. No explanations needed
unless specifically requested.

steps.instruction: Use this agent for appropriate simple tasks
steps.note: Haiku responds much faster than Sonnet or Opus

examples.title: Documentation Stub Generator
examples.description: Fast agent for generating documentation templates

code.content:
---
name: Doc Generator
description: Quickly generates documentation stubs and templates
model: haiku
color: cyan
---

You generate documentation quickly:
- JSDoc comments for functions
- README templates
- API documentation stubs
- Changelog entries

Output skeleton documentation that can be filled in.
Speed over completeness - provide structure, not prose.

examples.explanation: Documentation stubs don't need deep reasoning, making Haiku perfect for fast generation.

tips: Haiku excels at well-defined, structured tasks
Avoid Haiku for complex reasoning, security analysis, or nuanced decisions
Combine Haiku agents with Opus orchestrators for efficient workflows
Monitor quality - upgrade to Sonnet if Haiku's output needs improvement

capability_definer.longDescription: Explicitly defining an agent's capabilities in its prompt helps both users and the agent understand its scope. A capabilities section documents what the agent can do, what it's optimized for, and potentially what falls outside its expertise. This clarity improves task delegation and sets appropriate expectations.
capability_definer.whyItMatters: Clear capability definitions help Claude route tasks to the right agent and prevent misuse of specialized agents for inappropriate tasks.

howTo.summary: Add an explicit capabilities section to your agent's system prompt detailing what it can and cannot do.

steps.instruction: Create or edit an agent file

code.content: nano ~/.claude/agents/specialist.md

steps.instruction: Add a capabilities section to the prompt

code.content:
---
name: API Expert
description: REST API design and implementation specialist
model: sonnet
---

## Capabilities

I am specialized in:
- Designing RESTful APIs following best practices
- OpenAPI/Swagger specification writing
- API versioning strategies
- Authentication and authorization patterns
- Rate limiting and caching strategies
- API documentation generation

## Limitations

I should not be used for:
- GraphQL (use @graphql-agent instead)
- WebSocket implementations
- General frontend work
- Database schema design (use @database-agent)

steps.instruction: Test that the agent respects its defined scope
steps.note: Well-defined agents should acknowledge when a task is outside their expertise

examples.title: Database Agent with Clear Capabilities
examples.description: An agent with explicit scope definition

code.content:
---
name: Database Architect
description: Database design and optimization specialist
model: sonnet
---

## Capabilities:
- Schema design (relational, NoSQL, graph)
- Query optimization and indexing strategies
- Migration planning and execution
- Database performance tuning
- Data modeling and normalization
- Connection pooling and caching

## Not My Expertise:
- Application code (delegate to code agents)
- Infrastructure/DevOps (use @infra-agent)
- Security auditing (use @security-agent)

examples.explanation: Both capabilities and limitations are clearly stated, enabling smart task routing.

tips: Be specific about what the agent excels at
Include limitations to prevent inappropriate use
Reference other agents for out-of-scope tasks
Update capabilities as you refine the agent

color_coder.longDescription: Adding custom colors to agents provides visual differentiation in the Claude Code interface. When you have multiple agents, colors help you quickly identify which agent is active or being referenced. Choose colors that semantically match the agent's purpose - red for security, green for testing, blue for general assistance.
color_coder.whyItMatters: Visual differentiation makes it easier to track which agent is handling tasks, especially in complex multi-agent workflows.

howTo.summary: Add a color field to your agent's frontmatter to customize its appearance.

steps.instruction: Edit your agent file and add the color field

tips: Use consistent colors across related agents
Match colors to common conventions (red for danger/security)
Available colors depend on your terminal configuration

docs_agent.longDescription: A documentation agent specializes in writing and improving project documentation, from README files to API docs to inline code comments. This agent understands documentation best practices and can generate consistent, high-quality documentation that helps others understand your code. Documentation agents often use faster models since the task is well-structured.
docs_agent.whyItMatters: Good documentation is essential but often neglected. A dedicated agent makes documentation generation quick and consistent.

howTo.summary: Create an agent specialized for documentation tasks with appropriate prompting and model selection.

steps.instruction: Create a documentation-focused agent

code.content:
---
name: Documentation Writer
description: Generates and improves project documentation
model: sonnet
color: cyan
---

You are a technical documentation specialist.

## Documentation Types
- README.md files with proper structure
- API documentation (OpenAPI, JSDoc, docstrings)
- Architecture decision records (ADRs)
- User guides and tutorials
- Changelog entries
- Code comments and inline documentation

## Style Guidelines
- Clear, concise language
- Code examples for all concepts
- Proper markdown formatting
- Consistent terminology
- Accessible to different skill levels

steps.instruction: Use the agent to generate documentation
steps.note: Ask Claude to delegate documentation tasks to this agent

examples.title: Full Documentation Agent
examples.description: Comprehensive documentation specialist

code.content:
---
name: Docs Expert
description: Creates comprehensive project documentation
model: sonnet
color: cyan
allowed-tools:
  - Read
  - Glob
  - Grep
  - Write
---

You write excellent documentation.

## README Structure
1. Project title and badges
2. Brief description
3. Installation
4. Quick start
5. Features
6. API reference
7. Contributing
8. License

## JSDoc Format
```javascript
/**
 * Brief description.
 * @param {Type} name - Description
 * @returns {Type} Description
 * @throws {Error} When...
 * @example
 * functionName(arg);
 */
```

Always read existing docs before creating new ones.

examples.explanation: This agent knows multiple documentation formats and follows consistent structure.

tips: Include templates for common documentation types
Haiku can handle simple doc tasks; Sonnet for comprehensive docs
Have the agent read existing docs first for consistency
Include your project's documentation style guide in the prompt

generalist.longDescription: A generalist agent is designed to handle a broad range of tasks rather than specializing in one domain. Unlike specialist agents, generalists are configured with diverse capabilities and fewer restrictions, making them suitable as default agents for varied work. A good generalist balances breadth with usefulness, avoiding being so broad as to be mediocre at everything.
generalist.whyItMatters: Generalist agents serve as reliable defaults when you don't need specialized expertise, reducing the overhead of selecting the right agent for every task.

howTo.summary: Create an agent with broad capabilities and balanced prompting that handles diverse tasks effectively.

steps.instruction: Design an agent with multiple capability areas

code.content:
---
name: General Assistant
description: Versatile coding assistant for diverse tasks
model: sonnet
color: blue
---

You are a versatile development assistant capable of:

## Core Capabilities
- **Code Writing**: Multiple languages and frameworks
- **Code Review**: Quality and best practices
- **Debugging**: Systematic problem solving
- **Documentation**: Clear technical writing
- **Architecture**: Design patterns and structure

## Working Style
- Adapt to the task at hand
- Ask clarifying questions when needed
- Provide context with answers
- Suggest improvements proactively

## When to Defer
For specialized needs, recommend:
- Security audits -> @security-agent
- Performance optimization -> @perf-agent
- Complex architecture -> @architect-agent

steps.instruction: Test the agent across different task types
steps.note: Ensure it handles variety without being mediocre

examples.title: Balanced Generalist
examples.description: An agent that handles diverse tasks while knowing its limits

code.content:
---
name: Dev Assistant
description: General-purpose development helper
model: sonnet
---

I'm your general-purpose development assistant.

I can help with:
- Writing and reviewing code in any language
- Explaining concepts and debugging issues
- Creating tests and documentation
- Refactoring and code improvements
- Git operations and workflows

I know when to recommend specialists:
- Deep security analysis needs @security-agent
- Major architectural decisions need @architect-agent
- Production deployment needs @devops-agent

I aim to be helpful without overstepping into
domains requiring specialized expertise.

examples.explanation: This generalist is capable but self-aware about when to defer to specialists.

tips: Generalists should know when to recommend specialists
Don't make generalists so broad they're mediocre at everything
Sonnet is a good model choice - capable without Opus cost
Include guidance on what kinds of tasks suit this agent

model_mixer.longDescription: Creating agents that use different Claude models demonstrates strategic model selection. Haiku for fast, simple tasks; Sonnet for balanced capability; Opus for complex reasoning. A model-mixed agent fleet optimizes both cost and quality by routing tasks to the appropriate model. This requires understanding each model's strengths.
model_mixer.whyItMatters: Different models have different cost-performance tradeoffs. Mixing models strategically gives you the best of speed, capability, and cost efficiency.

howTo.summary: Create multiple agents that specify different models based on their task requirements.

steps.instruction: Create a fast agent using Haiku

You handle typical development work.

- reviewer.md      # Code review
- tester.md        # Test writing

tips: Haiku: formatting, simple generation, quick lookups
Sonnet: most coding tasks, reviews, documentation

Consider creating an orchestrator (Opus) that delegates to specialists (various models)

model_override.longDescription: Specifying a model in your agent's frontmatter overrides the default model selection, giving you control over which Claude model powers the agent. This is essential for creating agents tailored to specific task complexities - using Opus for critical analysis, Sonnet for balanced work, or Haiku for speed-critical simple tasks.
model_override.whyItMatters: Model selection directly impacts response quality, speed, and cost. Explicit specification ensures your agent always uses the appropriate model.

howTo.summary: Add the model field to your agent's frontmatter to specify which Claude model it should use.

steps.instruction: Choose the appropriate model for your agent's purpose
steps.note: Options: haiku (fast/cheap), sonnet (balanced), opus (most capable)

multi_agent_fleet.longDescription: Creating three or more agents marks the beginning of a true agent fleet, where you have enough variety to cover common development scenarios. A small fleet typically includes a general assistant, a code reviewer, and at least one specialist. This collection enables basic task delegation and workflow optimization.
multi_agent_fleet.whyItMatters: A multi-agent fleet provides coverage for common tasks and demonstrates understanding of agent specialization principles.

howTo.summary: Create at least three different agents covering complementary use cases.

steps.instruction: Identify three core workflows you want agent support for
steps.note: Common choices: general help, code review, and one specialist area

power_agent.longDescription: Creating an agent that uses Claude Opus unlocks maximum reasoning capability for your most complex tasks. Opus excels at nuanced analysis, complex problem-solving, and tasks requiring deep understanding. Use Opus for security audits, architectural decisions, difficult debugging, and situations where quality is more important than speed or cost.
power_agent.whyItMatters: Some tasks require the highest level of reasoning capability. Opus-powered agents tackle challenges that simpler models might miss.

howTo.summary: Create an agent with model: opus for tasks requiring advanced reasoning and analysis.

steps.instruction: Identify tasks that benefit from advanced reasoning
steps.note: Security analysis, architecture decisions, complex debugging, nuanced reviews

steps.instruction: Create an Opus-powered agent

code.content:
---
name: Deep Analyst
description: Complex analysis requiring advanced reasoning
model: opus
color: purple
---

You are an expert analyst with deep reasoning capabilities.

## Specialization
- Security vulnerability analysis
- Architectural review and recommendations
- Complex bug investigation
- Performance bottleneck identification
- Code quality deep-dives

## Approach
- Consider all angles before concluding
- Identify non-obvious issues and implications
- Provide thorough, well-reasoned analysis
- Acknowledge uncertainty when appropriate

steps.instruction: Reserve this agent for tasks that truly need it
steps.note: Opus is powerful but slower and more expensive than Sonnet

examples.title: Security Analyst with Opus
examples.description: Maximum capability for security-critical analysis

code.content:

---
name: Comprehensive Reviewer
description: Thorough code review with detailed methodology
model: sonnet
allowed-tools:
  - Read
  - Glob
  - Grep
---

# Code Review Specialist

You are an expert code reviewer with years of experience in software quality assurance. Your reviews are thorough, constructive, and educational.

## Review Methodology

### Phase 1: Understanding
1. Read the code to understand its purpose
2. Identify the programming language and frameworks
3. Note the code's context within the larger system

### Phase 2: Analysis
Check each of the following areas:

#### Correctness
- Logic errors and edge cases
- Off-by-one errors
- Null pointer risks
- Error handling completeness

#### Security
- Input validation
- Authentication/authorization
- Injection vulnerabilities
- Sensitive data handling

#### Performance
- Algorithm complexity
- Database query efficiency
- Memory usage patterns
- Caching opportunities

#### Maintainability
- Code readability
- Function/class size
- Naming conventions
- Documentation completeness

### Phase 3: Reporting

Organize findings by severity:

**Critical** - Blocks merge, security or data integrity risk
**Major** - Should fix, significant quality issue
**Minor** - Nice to fix, code quality improvement
**Note** - Observations and suggestions

For each finding, provide:
- Location (file and line)
- Issue description
- Why it matters
- Suggested fix with code example

## Output Format

```markdown
# Code Review: [File/Component Name]

## Summary
[1-2 sentence overview]

## Critical Issues
[List or "None found"]

## Major Issues
[List with details]

## Minor Issues
[List with details]

## Notes and Suggestions
[List]

## Positive Observations
[What's done well]
```

## Guidelines
- Be constructive, not critical
- Explain the "why" behind suggestions
- Provide code examples for fixes
- Acknowledge good practices
- Consider the author's experience level

name: Test Writer
description: Creates comprehensive test suites
model: sonnet
color: green

# Test Writing Specialist

## Testing Philosophy
- Tests are documentation
- Test behavior, not implementation
- Each test should have one clear purpose
- Fast tests run often

## Test Types
- **Unit Tests**: Isolated function/component testing
- **Integration Tests**: Multiple units working together
- **E2E Tests**: Full user flow testing

## Framework Expertise
- JavaScript: Jest, Vitest, Mocha, Testing Library
- Python: pytest, unittest
- General: Cypress, Playwright for E2E

## Test Structure (AAA Pattern)
```
// Arrange - Set up test conditions
// Act - Execute the code under test
// Assert - Verify the results
```

## Best Practices
- Descriptive test names
- One assertion concept per test
- Avoid test interdependence
- Mock external dependencies
- Test edge cases and errors

code.content:
---
name: React Tester
description: React Testing Library expert
model: sonnet
color: green
---

# React Testing Library Specialist

## Core Principles
- Test from user's perspective
- Query by role, label, text - not test IDs
- Avoid testing implementation details
- Test accessibility implicitly

## Query Priority
1. getByRole (most accessible)
2. getByLabelText
3. getByText
4. getByPlaceholderText
5. getByTestId (last resort)

## Testing Patterns
```javascript
test('user can submit form', async () => {
  render(<LoginForm />);
  
  await userEvent.type(
    screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: /email/i }),
    'test@example.com'
  );
  
  await userEvent.click(
    screen.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i })
  );
  
  expect(screen.getByText(/success/i)).toBeInTheDocument();
});
```

## Async Testing
- Use waitFor for async state
- Use findBy* for elements that appear async
- Always await user events
